sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Vision Statement**: The core philosophy of Technology Vision 2035 is 'Technology for the People' (Technological self-reliance ensuring socio-economic empowerment, security, and sustainable growth).
• **Institutional Architect**: Formulated by **TIFAC** (Technology Information, Forecasting and Assessment Council), an autonomous organization under the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)**.
• **Core Objectives**: Anticipating future technological requirements, mapping out R&D pathways, prioritizing indigenous capabilities, and linking technology foresight with national security, health, agriculture, and infrastructure.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Alignment of 12 technology domains with national imperatives such as Make in India, Digital India, Swachh Bharat, and sustainable climate goals.

items.definition: The systematic process of attempting to look longer-term into the future of science, technology, economy, and society with the aim of identifying the areas of strategic research and the emerging generic technologies likely to yield the greatest economic and social benefits.

items.term: TIFAC (Technology Information, Forecasting and Assessment Council)
items.definition: Established in 1988 under DST, it acts as India's premier think-tank for technology assessment and foresight, playing a pivotal role in formulating successive Technology Vision documents (Vision 2020 and Vision 2035).
The capability of a nation to design, develop, manufacture, and maintain critical technologies independently without being vulnerable to external supply-chain shocks or geopolitical coercions.
National Science, Technology and Innovation Policy (STIP), Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), and DST strategic roadmaps.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Technology Clusters & Innovation Belts**: Bengaluru-Hyderabad-Pune corridors for IT, aerospace, and advanced manufacturing; National Capital Region (NCR) for policy, electronics, and AI research.
• **Driving Advantages**: Proximity to premier IITs/IISc, availability of skilled demographic dividend, robust startup ecosystems, and dedicated government SEZs/Technology Parks.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Low Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD hovers around 0.7% of GDP), weak academia-industry linkage, bureaucratic inertia, and intellectual property (IP) commercialization hurdles.
• **Policy Interventions**: Boosting private sector R&D contribution, strengthening Anusandhan National Research Foundation (NRF), fostering deep-tech startups, and streamlining public procurement for indigenous innovations.

items.title: Mnemonic for Core Domains (PAW-HIM-WEE)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **PAW-HIM-WEE** (Power, Agriculture, Water / Health, Infrastructure, Materials / Waste, Environment, Education).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Represents the core human-centric focus areas of Technology Vision 2035.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly helps eliminate incorrect options in questions asking whether specific domains fall under the vision document.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember '35' in 2035 as the milestone year for a developed India ('Viksit Bharat'), moving backward from the 100th year of Independence (2047).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently attributes the Technology Vision Document to NITI Aayog or the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) directly. Always remember it is formulated by **TIFAC under the Department of Science and Technology (DST)**.

Mains Value Addition: Quote Technology Vision 2035 in answers related to R&D funding, Make in India, indigenous defense capabilities, and sustainable development goals (SDGs) to showcase multi-disciplinary analytical depth.

keyTakeaways: Technology Vision 2035 is an indigenous foresight exercise led by TIFAC to direct India's technological trajectory toward self-reliance.
It spans 12 critical socio-economic domains placing 'Technology for the People' at the center of development.
Bridging the gap between lab-scale research and commercial deployment remains the key implementation challenge for realizing this vision.
